reader.requirement: A VALUE clause on a group item is refused when any item subordinate to it (at any depth) is described with JUSTIFIED, SYNCHRONIZED, or a USAGE other than DISPLAY (1985 usages BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL, INDEX, PACKED-DECIMAL, written or inherited from a subordinate group's USAGE).
reader.edition-search: grep for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior in CheckGroupValueDeclarationsPass.cs and DataBinder.GroupValue.cs: only binder.Edition.At/Error (the diagnostic sink, EditionContext#Error, which records the error with no edition switch); the pass's doc states it is not dialect-gated.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f11_01 is one VALUE case; JUSTIFIED, SYNCHRONIZED LEFT, each non-DISPLAY usage, inherited group USAGE and a grandchild were exercised only by these probes

probes.printed: COBOL1702 for J1 (JUSTIFIED), S1 (SYNCHRONIZED), SL1 (SYNC LEFT), C1 (COMP), B1 (BINARY), P1 (PACKED-DECIMAL), I1 (INDEX), N2 (COMPUTATIONAL two levels down), U1 (COMP inherited from group GU1)

probes.expected: groups whose subordinates are all DISPLAY (explicit USAGE IS DISPLAY, nested group, OCCURS) accept the VALUE (nonnumeric literal, ALL literal, figurative ZEROS) and initialize the area

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.15.6 GR4  (5.15.6 Data Description Entries Other Than Condition-Names)  the text is in GR4

reader.notes: Every subordinate violation is refused with COBOL1702, inherited usage included (the pass runs after usage inheritance). The message names COMP as 'usage BINARY' and cites only §2023:13.18.63.3 SR14 at --std 85; that is diagnostic wording, not a failure of the rule. The groups declared with COMP also drew COBOL1740 (literal longer than the group) because the probe's literals were sized for display.

refuter.evidence: cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.15.6 GR4. Read CheckGroupValueDeclarationsPass#Run/#Subordinates/#SubordinateUsageOf: whole-subtree walk after usage inheritance, no edition arm. Probes at --std 85: grpv2bad.cob refuses COBOL1702 for a REDEFINES subordinate with COMP (R2), a FILLER COMP, SYNCHRONIZED RIGHT and JUST RIGHT under an OCCURS group; grpv2.cob/grpv3.cob accept a group VALUE over SIGN LEADING SEPARATE, BLANK WHEN ZERO, numeric-edited, a level-88 and a REDEFINES subordinate (none of which GR4 forbids). SEPARATE FINDING (not this rule): grpv3.cob/grpv4.cob show the group VALUE SILENTLY DROPPED whenever a subordinate has REDEFINES: `01 G3 VALUE "ABCD". 05 A3 PIC X(4). 05 A4 REDEFINES A3 PIC X(4).` displays G3=[    ] (expected ABCD); `01 G5 VALUE "1234". 05 C3 PIC 9(4). 05 C4 REDEFINES C3 PIC X(4).` displays [0000]; same at --std 2023. That violates §1985:VI.5.15.6 GR3 (cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.15.6 GR3 'the group area is initialized without consideration for the individual elementary or group items'); the VALUE is legal since GR2 bars VALUE only in the REDEFINES entry and its subordinates. No kb/Work note found (grep for group VALUE with REDEFINES).
